additional_info.body:
Hello RC-PK Team,
I trust this email finds you in good health. We have received a technical support request from
Siemens Pakistan Engeneering Co.
in your region regarding the following product:
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
MP / NN 170000080
Charger ID/Serial No.:
Ck6muI
Problem Description:
DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 error.
Kindly go onsite and check the plug. In particular, please check the status of the pins of the plug and the connector mating surface. Please check if dust or dirt is inside the fins of the plug, or if the fins are bent/broken. All these points might reduce the contact surface or create hotspots, resulting in CableTempSensor issue.
The Active error flag on SCB is below:
VIV:0 CCE:0 RNE:1 PLE:0 SOV:0 COV:0 CBL:0 KON:1 CAB:0 HOU:0
The following values show the error state (OK state would be the negated value):
VIV:0 → in case of an invalid sensor reading
RNE:1 → in case of a sensor reading outside the defined operation range
KON:1: → in case the contact temperature sensors are not okay
We will recommend you the following steps to be followed
1. Check resistance between P1 and P2, N1 and N2 in below attached image, and check at the XD101.
2. Connectivity between P2 & N2.
3. Please check the KF13 wirings.
Upon reviewing our asset database, we found that the product is no longer under warranty since [11/8/2023], as a result, we are transferring the case to the regional queue.
Kindly communicate with the customer and provide the necessary service support and/or offer. We have already informed the customer that a regional representative will be in touch shortly.
Should you require further remote or expert support, please order it via PMD.
For additional information, please visit the Service Collaboration SharePoint. If you need assistance with ordering Expert Support, feel free to reach out to Sousa, Afonso (SI E CS SD) at
afonso-sousa@siemens.com
or Teodoso, Rui (SI E CS SD ES) at

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0419755-DC/Si-D/PK-[MP / NN 170000080] DC2 out of order CRM:02023000583
additional_info.body:
Good evening Adnan,
Attached to this email you can find the report of today's ExpertNow Service.
Today during the support call, we observed that the charger
Ck6muI
was not able to complete the booting phase, as it remained stuck at 30%. Since the charger was not able to boot up, the remote connection to SCB could not be established, hence any remote activity and troubleshooting was not possible.
I understood that the End customer switches off and powers on the charger overnight daily, and I assessed that this shutdown procedure was not done correctly. Most likely, during an incorrect shutdown phase the FW of the charger got corrupted, hence it is necessary to re-commission the charger.
I already shared with you the correct procedure in order to switch off and on the charger, I will copy the steps here for your convenience:
Open the door
On the HMI it will appear a button “shutdown station”. Press it
To restart the station, press twice FC12
Close the door
In case these steps were not possible for whatever reason (HMI issue, charger stuck, etc), this is the correct procedure to switch off/reboot the charger:
Open the door
Put the dip-switch of PLC KF1 into STOP position
Press FC12
Switch off breaker QA2
Switch on breaker QA2
Put the dip-switch of PLC KF1 into RUN position
Press FC12
Close the door
It is important NOT to cut the power supply to the PLC before setting the PLC into STOP position.
The risk otherwise is to damage the FW. Please make the End customer aware of this procedure.
In order to proceed further with the investigation, we need to recommission the charger. To do so, we have to flash the FW on the CFast Card and prepare the Live Linux USB Stick. These are the SW tools and steps that we will need to perform tomorrow (invitation for preparation support sent for 12:00 CET).
HW Tools:
Laptop With Admin Rights.
Should be able to access dual network (Both ethernet/Wifi)
Ethernet cables
1 USB 64 GB
CFast Card Reader
1 External Keyboard with USB connection
Electric ties
Multimeter (for further troubleshooting)
General working tools
SW Tools:
Any SW for flashing images (HDDRawCopy, balenaEtcher, rufus, etc)
Sicharge D Companion
Software:
​​​​​​​
Live Linux image (shared already via Secufex)
Config file of the charger (shared already via Secufex)​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
Sicharge D FW v6.1.3 or v7.0.5, to be downloaded in Sicharge D Companion, under “Firmware Management” section.
Preparation
:
​​​​​​​
Download the firmware image (v7.0.5 or v6.1.3) from Companion. Please make sure to have at least 90 GB free.
Connect the CFast card to the laptop via CFast Card reader and, via Companion, flash the downloaded FW.
Download the Live Linux Image file shared via Secufex (1,8GB) and extract it (32 GB)
Flash the Live Linux image on a USB driver
Once flashed, configure the Live Linux USB with the config files shared and the correct script.
Go to the charger and perform the recommissioning by:
Insert the USB (Cfast card out, plc in stop, charger off)
PLC to run
Put the Cfast card in the slot (but don't insert it, don't push it)
Turn on the charger
Follow instruction on the HMI
I will support you tomorrow to prepare the CFast Card and Live Linux USB and to recommission the charger.
In order to save time, it would be important if, before our meeting, you could download the FW from Companion and download and extract the Live Linux Image.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0419755-DC/Si-D/PK-[MP / NN 170000080] DC2 out of order CRM:02023000583
additional_info.body:
Good evening colleagues,
I am reaching out to summarize the status of the activities for charger
CkSmuI
in Pakistan. Yesterday (19.05.2025), we finally managed to flash the FW v6.1.3 on the CFast card, by using a laptop with Windows 10 version. From service side we will investigate on possible issues in flashing CFast cards when using Windows 11 and in case advise the service community.
Today (20.05.2025), the colleagues went onsite, and I supported them to recommission the charger. The recommissioning went successful, but unfortunately the charger entered in a boot-loop.
After 4 booting phases, the charger went finally online, and it came up in FAILSAFE mode.
The charger enters the failsafe mode whenever the communication to one of the vital controllers is permanently lost (routers, EcoGs, PLC). I analyzed the error flags and the logs and we connected locally to the charger, and we found out that the EcoG-Main KF11 is not communicating with the charger. The EcoG-LE KF12 is instead communicating correctly.
You can see in the images below that the KF11 did not perform the update (during recommissioning), and that the IP 10.20.17.100 is not visible.
We also tried to power-cycle the KF11, and to change the ethernet cable, but the communication was never re-established. Therefore, it is necessary to replace the KF11, in order to exit the failsafe mode and to complete the update.
The component to order is the following:
